newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spy put money into gold, mutual funds.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spy put money into gold, mutual funds.

text.p: Where does a spy put his ill-gotten loot?

In the case of Harold James Nicholson, the former CIA case officer who pleaded guilty and is in jail awaiting sentencing for spying for Russia, he apparently put his money into everything from mutual funds to spy novels.

In a forfeiture order filed with the U.S. District Court in Alexandria, Va., that was made public on Thursday, the government listed what Nicholson did with about $300,000 he got for passing papers to the Russians.

The government will now get his valuables that included mutual fund investments such as The Kaufman Fund, USAA's International Fund and its World Growth Fund, the Templeton Developing Markets Trust and Franklin Convertible Securities Fund.

The order also said he had a secret bank account in Switzerland and eight gold coins, gold necklaces, a home, a Rolex watch, a stamp and coin collection, five guns, a leather-bound collection of novels of Louis L'Amour, the late Western writer, and books by spy writer Ian Fleming.
In addition to computers, furniture, oriental rugs and other items were a king-size brass bed with a baked enamel inscription that said "especially handcrafted for Batman," apparently his nickname.
